## Proposed change
<!--

  maintainers why we should accept this pull request. If it fixes a bug

Login requests with invalid credentials are currently returned with HTTP status code 200.
I propose to return the IMO more correct status code 401 Unauthorized on all invalid logins.

This allows the user e.g. to block requests with fail2ban on a network level after too many (=user defined) failed login requests.

issue_context.title: HA returns HTTP status code 200 on login with bad credentials
issue_context.body:
### The problem

Hi,

I just noticed that Home Assistant returns a response with HTTP status code 200 on a bad login request with invalid credentials.
This seems a bit unexpected and makes blocking attackers e.g. with fail2ban harder as I can't just filter failed requests based on 4xx status codes.

The correct HTTP status code to return would be 401, see https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Status/401
> ... the client request has not been completed because it lacks valid authentication credentials for the requested resource

It seems to be somehow intended according to the tests here
https://github.com/home-assistant/core/blob/14f68ec1a92ac7e41a1340f76255d6596affdd15/tests/components/auth/test_login_flow.py#L42-L53

Is this really intended?

Thanks for looking into this!

### What version of Home Assistant Core has the issue?

2022.9.6

I think tests mainly verify current behaviour here. However in this case the request did complete, albeit with a negative response, so its not clear that 401 should be used in that case.

You should be getting 401 if you request things protected. This service is per say not protected.

Im not entirely sure what the standard says here.

> This service is per say not protected.

I'm not exactly sure what you mean here, I mean the HTTP status code does not change anything with regards to HAs security.

It might make sense that this was simply not considered during the initial implementation as you say, maybe someone senior with regards to this implementation knows more.

review_comments: I expect this assertion to fail. The method is already decorated with `@log_invalid_auth` so the call to `await process_wrong_login(request)` when the status code is overridden is now logging a wrong login a 2nd time.
Is this still needed? the comment mentioned it was not working because we returned a 200 but now we return a 401.

This is actually the most important line of this PR if I didn't misunderstand :).
Previously everything was just HTTPStatus.OK as this is the default value in `_prepare_result_json` for the optional status code param.
This overwrites this behaviour in the bad credential case.
